stem.en: An atom has four pairs of electrons around it, all shared. Kabir says the four bonds "lie flat in a cross, ninety degrees each". Why is that wrong?

text.en: A flat cross keeps the pairs closer together than a pyramid does. Four pairs pushing apart end up at the corners of a triangular pyramid, about 109 degrees apart, because that is the furthest four things can get from each other around a point.
Because atoms are round, so bonds must curve.

feedback.en: The bonds are straight lines from the centre. The question is which directions, and repulsion answers it: the pyramid, not the cross.

text.en: Because a flat cross would need five pairs.

feedback.en: The centre is the nucleus, not a pair. Four pairs make four arms. The issue is that four flat arms are not as far apart as four pyramid arms.
Ninety degrees is a real angle between some bonds in some solids. It is wrong here because the four balloons can get further apart than that.

explanation.en: On a flat cross, each balloon has two neighbours at 90 degrees. Tilt them into a pyramid, and each has three neighbours at 109 degrees. More space for everyone. Repulsion picks the pyramid.
